entries.review_note: Sudō declines physical retaliation against Class A bullying despite verbal anger; the motive for restraint is uncertain.
Ike's team locates river and site mechanics, but group exploration prevents attributing every discovery to him alone.
Ike corrects damp thick fuel by gathering tinder and lights the bonfire; direct task-specific outdoor skill.
Ike directly apologizes to Shinohara and she responds; episode-level regret, not fixed temperament.
Sudō offers boiling as a compromise in water conflict; neither purification nor compliance is independently tested.
Hirata argues a purchased toilet avoids queue, privacy and sanitation problems; eventual collective consent is evidenced.
Hirata computes a contingent 120-point target; no guarantee it equals 225 final score.
Hirata grants Ibuki shelter conditionally; her covert identity makes his belief reliability distinct from compassionate action.
Hirata privately suppresses public discovery of Kiyotaka's underwear possession, not a formal acquittal.
Hirata becomes briefly unresponsive in crisis, with an unelaborated allusion to past events; limit to this observed breakdown.
Kushida's willingness to volunteer triggers volunteers but others' motives differ, so avoid guaranteeing universal persuasion.
Kushida nominates Suzune as secret leader; Hirata actually submits name and delivers card, keeping action ownership separate.
Kushida coordinates four friends sharing scarce rations to assist Ibuki; source locates handoff on PDF p96.
Suzune accepts designated leader role with hidden keycard, not prior awareness of replacement exception.
Suzune admits outdoors skills can compensate for academics; expressed reevaluation is not lasting character transformation.
Fever seriously compromises Suzune's duel with Ibuki; result does not rank healthy Suzune below Ibuki.
Suzune privately discloses lost keycard to Kiyotaka and asks help; her trust is actor-scoped.
Sakura volunteers to accompany group for collecting wood despite fatigue and difficult social context.
Sakura notices cultivated corn first and Kiyotaka independently infers its artificial planting; roles remain distinct.
Sakura defends Kiyotaka amid theft suspicions but retreats when Karuizawa attacks her socially.
Katsuragi, not Kiyotaka, directly describes ship-path deduction to Yahiko while Kiyotaka overhears; cave occupancy is shared.
Kiyotaka pauses after spotting an injured outsider and offers support; Ibuki's covert motive is not known at that instant.
Kiyotaka uses his shirt as temporary harvest carrier; group later recovers corn, no general engineering inference.
Kiyotaka accepts Ike's handed underwear and conceals it before Hirata searches; does not itself solve the theft.
Kiyotaka suspects Ibuki based on gaze and misplaced underwear; she has not confessed to him yet.
Kiyotaka locates, carries and presents unconscious Suzune under severe rain, including a fall, with bounded protection.
Kiyotaka exploits a medically justified replacement after actual retirement; opponents' prior identity guesses no longer match.
Kiyotaka offers aid conditional on Suzune not probing his past; handshake is a present agreement only.
Ryūen directs conspicuous luxury resources in C camp; hidden political bargain is not proven by spending alone.
Ryūen dismissively throws back Ishizaki's water and intimidates him; obeying once is not stable loyalty.
Ibuki actually delivers the card to Ryūen and Katsuragi, participates in accepted alliance and later returns it; contract price hidden.
Ibuki defeats a febrile Suzune, but Ibuki herself notes healthy result could differ; avoid absolute combat ranking.
Ichinose explains collective Class B well-testing procedure; she is not proved the person who personally performed tests.
Katsuragi argues unspoken mutual nonintrusion after Horikita tests cave boundaries; it is not a formal school-wide law.
Chabashira uses unverified family expulsion allegation as leverage; observed pressure differs from actual unilateral removal power.
